name: Black-Eyed Pea Salad With Corn and Tangy Coconut Dressing

ingredients.name: coconut milk, can well-shaken before opening
kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste

instructions.primary_message: Finely chop the palm sugar. Grate the zest from the lime. Juice the lime. Finely chop the red onion. Core and cut the ripe plum into 1/2-inch pieces. Chop the red bell pepper. Chop the green bell pepper. Drain and rinse the black-eyed peas.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp palm sugar
1 tsp lime zest
1 lime, divided
1 small red onion
2 ripe plum
1 medium red bell pepper
1 medium green bell pepper
1 (439 g) can black-eyed peas

instructions.primary_message: For the Dressing: In a small saucepan, combine palm sugar and coconut aminos. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until sugar is dissolved, 4 to 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and whisk in coconut milk, coconut vinegar or apple cider vinegar, and cayenne. Set aside and let cool completely.

For the Salad: In a large bowl, whisk together lime juice and 1 teaspoon kosher salt until salt dissolves. Add onion and jalapeño and let sit for 10 minutes. Add tomatoes, red and green bell peppers, black-eyed peas or black beans, corn, coconut, cilantro stems, lime zest, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt and toss to combine.
Add 1/3 cup dressing and toss well. Taste and season with additional salt as needed. If serving cold, cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Transfer to a serving bowl and top with cilantro leaves. Top with shredded coconut and/or plantain chips, if using. Serve with remaining dressing on the side.

description: This quick, make-ahead black-eyed pea salad combines sweet corn, coconut, tomatoes, peppers, and lime with a tangy coconut dressing.
notes:
Optional substitutions: finely chopped palm sugar → light brown sugar; coconut vinegar → apple cider vinegar; red onion → white onion; ripe plum → Roma tomatoes or off-the-vine tomatoes; black-eyed peas → black beans

Notes: Coconut aminos are a dark, savory-sweet seasoning made from coconut sap. They’re typically sold near soy sauce and other Asian condiments at well-stocked supermarkets, natural-food stores, and online. In place of the coconut aminos, use 2 tablespoons light soy sauce mixed with 2 tablespoons water.
The salad can be served warm, at room temperature, or chilled.

Make-ahead and storage: The dressing can be made up to 1 week ahead and refrigerated in an airtight container. Shake well before using.
The salad can be made up to 2 days ahead and refrigerated in an airtight container; add the cilantro leaves, toasted shredded coconut, and plantain chips, if using, just before serving.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Ozoz Sokoh
